set_text.text: Cost per delivery is the share of a route day that one stop uses up, whatever it carries. It comes from the day's driver, fuel and truck costs, split evenly across every drop. It is the cost a delivery minimum has to clear.
The route day and nothing before it. Picking in the warehouse and the time spent taking the order sit outside the $27.18, so serving a stop costs more.
The calculator splits the day evenly, but a long unload or a detour uses more of the 8 hours than a quick drop.
The order that misses the route
An order that arrives after the route is built waits a day or gets a trip of its own. A trip of its own puts driver time, fuel and the truck behind one drop.
Who uses a delivery cost calculator
It is for distributors that deliver on their own trucks, from one route to a full fleet. Whoever sets the minimum, quotes a new stop or cuts a route should have the number.
